title: Mumbai Biker Riddhi Thakkar Dies in Hit-and-Run During All-Women Group Ride
excerpt: The 24-year-old Mumbai woman was killed when a speeding truck rammed her motorcycle on NH-30 in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district while she was on a group ride with 22 other women bikers.
body:
• Riddhi Thakkar, 24, from Mumbai was killed in a hit-and-run crash on NH-30 in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district
  • She was part of an all-women group motorcycle ride with 22 other women bikers touring the Bastar region
  • A speeding trailer rammed her motorcycle from behind; the truck driver fled the scene
  • The incident has reignited concerns about road safety on national highways and the vulnerability of two-wheeler riders

Riddhi Thakkar, a 24-year-old motorcycle enthusiast from Mumbai, was killed in a hit-and-run crash on National Highway 30 in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district while participating in an all-women group motorcycle ride, according to the Times of India.

Thakkar was riding with a group of 22 women bikers touring the Bastar region when a speeding trailer struck her motorcycle from behind. She died from her injuries, while the truck driver fled the scene. Police have registered a case and launched a search for the driver.

A Passion Cut Short

Thakkar was known in Mumbai's biking community as an avid motorcyclist who had participated in several group rides across India. The all-women Bastar tour was organized to promote women's participation in long-distance motorcycle touring, a growing movement in India that has gained visibility through social media and biking clubs.

Fellow riders from the group described the moment of the crash as sudden and devastating. The trailer reportedly struck Thakkar's motorcycle without warning on a stretch of NH-30 known for heavy truck traffic and poor lighting conditions.

Road Safety Concerns

The incident has renewed attention on the dangers facing two-wheeler riders on India's national highways. According to government data, two-wheeler riders account for roughly 44% of all road accident fatalities in India, with hit-and-run cases involving trucks and heavy vehicles among the most lethal scenarios.

NH-30 runs through heavily forested terrain in Chhattisgarh, and stretches through Bastar have been flagged by road safety advocates as accident-prone due to a combination of speeding trucks, poor road markings, and limited emergency response infrastructure.

"She was living her dream. The ride was supposed to be about freedom and empowerment. Instead, we lost her to a reckless truck driver who didn't even stop."

— Fellow rider from the group

The Chhattisgarh government recently partnered with IIT Madras to scientifically identify accident-prone stretches and introduce targeted interventions at black spots across the state. The data-driven road safety program will begin in the state's 10 most accident-prone districts.

Women Bikers in India

India's women biking community has grown rapidly in recent years, with organized group rides becoming a powerful symbol of independence and adventure. Events like the all-women Bastar ride attract participants from across the country and have helped challenge traditional gender norms around motorcycling.

Thakkar's death has prompted an outpouring of tributes from the biking community on social media, with riders calling for stricter enforcement against hit-and-run drivers and better highway safety infrastructure for motorcyclists.

Police said they are reviewing CCTV footage from nearby toll plazas and petrol stations to identify the trailer involved in the crash. A case has been registered under sections related to rash driving, causing death by negligence, and fleeing the scene of an accident.
